pr_title: Fix get_string_size not recognizing tab character + Added tab spacing equal to 4 spaces.
pr_body:
Fix #38315
As per issue, added special case for handling tab character, set equal to 4 spaces.
pr_comments: @kopcion Is this still desired? If so, it needs to be [rebased](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/community/contributing/pr_workflow.html#the-interactive-rebase) and tested on the latest master branch. Additionally, the above feedback needs to be addressed (in this case we can just do `ret.width += 4 * spacing_space + spacing_char;`).

I can confirm that #38315 is still reproducible in latest `master`.

```
	print(get_theme_font("font").get_string_size("Hello"))
	print(get_theme_font("font").get_string_size("Hell\to"))
	print(get_theme_font("font").get_string_size("Hell	o"))
	print(get_theme_font("font").get_string_size("Hell    o"))
```
returns
```
(39, 23)
(39, 23)
(39, 23)
(55, 23)
```
in a `TextEdit` with default theme.

In 4.x there's `tab_align` function in the `TextLine` and `TextParagraph` to align tabs in context, which is used by `TextEdit` for example.

`Font` functions like `draw_string` and `get_string_size` will use tab character width from the font, which is usually zero.

Hard-coding it to the arbitrary `4 * space` or any other constant value seems wrong to me. Even when indent width is set, the width of the specific tab is not a constant, e.g:
```
abcd    abc // 4 sapces
abcdef	abc // tab - looks like 2 spaces
abcde	abc // tab - looks like 3 spaces
abcd	abc // tab - looks like 4 spaces
abc	abc // tab - looks like 5 spaces
ab	abc // tab - looks like 6 spaces
a	abc // tab - looks like 7 spaces
```

I guess we can add an extra `tab_align` argument to the `draw_string`, `get_string_size` and multiline equivalents to apply the same alignment logic as `TextLine` and `TextParagraph`. But these functions already are a bit too complex, e.g `draw_multiline_string` have 11 arguments, maybe it's better to leave stuff like this to the `TextLine` and `TextParagraph`.

issue_context.title: get_string_size() and get_wordwrap_string_size() don't recognize the tab character.
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.1
**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10
**Issue description:**
In the TextEdit you can insert a TAB character into your text and it takes up space.  However if you test the size with `get_string_size()` or `get_wordwrap_string_size()`, you will get 0.  

the code `get_string_size("\t\tHello")` only returns the size of "Hello".
the code `get_wordwrap_string_size("\t\tHello\n", 100)` only returns the size of "Hello" and "\n".
comments:
I might be wrong here, but looking at the source code it seems to me that the problem might be in the font files, as there is no special handling of '\t' character. Instead, all the arithmetics is done by adding the width of consecutive chars and subtracting kerning. Also looking at the font files (godot/thirdparty/fonts/) it would seem they are provided from outside, as 'thirdparty' suggests.

If this is indeed a problem and not intended behaviour I can add something like this:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25220729/81509881-0ae7a580-930e-11ea-80da-87a5f8711c0e.png)

That would be great.
